headline: Presidential election held today after 35 years, with 349 MPs casting votes
summary: Bangladesh is holding its presidential election today, the first in 35 years with multiple candidates. Voting is taking place in the Jatiya Sangsad from 2 PM to 5 PM.
details: Bangladesh is holding its presidential election today, marking the first time in 35 years that multiple candidates are vying for the post. Voting is scheduled from 2 PM to 5 PM in the Jatiya Sangsad (National Parliament).

A total of 349 Members of Parliament (MPs) are eligible to cast their votes in this election. Although the outcome is largely predetermined, the presence of more than one candidate necessitates a vote.
The two candidates are Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, representing the ruling BNP, and Oli Ahmad, the candidate from an 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami.
With the BNP holding 247 seats in parliament, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir's election as president is virtually assured due to the significant numerical advantage.

headline_marked: [[Dipu Moni released on 12-hour parole]] to attend husband’s funeral
headline: Dipu Moni released on 12-hour parole to attend husband’s funeral
summary: Former minister Dr. Dipu Moni was granted a 12-hour parole from Munshiganj District Jail to pay her last respects to her husband, Tawfique Nawaz, who passed away at 76.
details: Former minister Dr. Dipu Moni, an Awami League leader, was released on a 12-hour parole from Munshiganj District Jail this morning. She was granted temporary freedom from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM to attend the funeral of her late husband.

Her daughter, Tani Dipabali, submitted an application to the Munshiganj deputy commissioner yesterday, seeking parole for her mother. The authorities subsequently approved the request, allowing her to participate in the final rites.

Dipu Moni's husband, Tawfique Nawaz, a Supreme Court lawyer, passed away at 76 on Tuesday night while undergoing treatment at Continental Hospital in Dhaka's Gulshan. He had been suffering from kidney and liver complications for an extended period.

Following her release, Dipu Moni will visit her residence in Dhaka's Kalabagan to pay her last respects. The namaz-e-janaza is scheduled to be held at Azad Mosque, after which he will be laid to rest at Banani Graveyard.
